submission.justification: Recommend Algorithm-L2 at 35 GeV because, among the three Level-1-eligible candidates and simulated thresholds, it gives the highest recorded signal efficiency at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate: 92.371%, exceeding the hard 80% efficiency requirement and outperforming Algorithm-L1 and Algorithm-L3 at the same/reference threshold. The threshold is within the allowed 20–60 GeV range. However, the recorded project documents did not provide a latency value for any candidate, so the hard Level-1 latency requirement of <=4.0 us is not verified from the available evidence.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate.
requirements.evidence: At the allocated_rate_khz = 8 and selected threshold 35 GeV, Algorithm-L2 has the highest recorded efficiency, 92.371%, compared with Algorithm-L1 at 74.712% and Algorithm-L3 at 82.6% in the coarse grid.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_count = 3; recommended option is Algorithm-L2, one of the listed candidates; level1_eligible_Algorithm_L2 = 1.

requirements.requirement: The signal efficiency at the allocated rate must be at least 80%.
requirements.evidence: recommended_efficiency_pct = 92.371, which is above the 80% hard requirement.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm's latency on the Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 us.
requirements.evidence: documented_latency_us_Algorithm_L2 = -1 and latency_documented_flag_Algorithm_L2 = 0; recommendation_latency_verified_le_4us = 0. No candidate has documented latency in the recorded results.
recommended_threshold_gev = 35, which lies within the allowed 20–60 GeV range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended algorithm and threshold.
requirements.evidence: Submitted one recommendation: Algorithm-L2 with threshold 35 GeV.
